summary:
What happens when fire leaves Earth?

We built FLARE UP to turn that question into an interactive journey through NASA’s microgravity combustion research. Watch the visual atmosphere shift between Earth and microgravity, ask questions about fire in space, and explore a Fire Lab that connects curiosity to real scientific evidence.

NASA has spent decades studying combustion beyond Earth. FLARE UP helps people explore that knowledge through accessible explanations, experiment comparisons and direct links to original sources. It also makes the limits visible: what research reports, what it may suggest and what remains unknown.

Created for Flame in Freefall, FLARE UP brings complex spacecraft fire research closer to students, educators and curious explorers. Our goal is to spark understanding of a challenge that matters wherever humans travel next: understanding fire when everyday intuition no longer applies.
details:
WHY WE BUILT FLARE UP

NASA has accumulated valuable microgravity combustion research, but finding relevant experiments and comparing their conditions can be difficult. We built FLARE UP to make that evidence accessible through an interactive web experience for students, educators and research explorers.

THREE WAYS TO EXPLORE

"Ask FLARE UP" lets users ask questions in everyday language. Our evidence engine routes questions to scientific text, structured measurements, or both. Optional Groq synthesis turns retrieved evidence into concise, cited explanations; source excerpts remain available when synthesis is unavailable. Reported findings, interpretation and what is not established remain distinct. Numerical answers come from source records, not generated guesses.

Fire Lab lets users explore gravity, oxygen, pressure, airflow, airflow direction and sample type through an interactive 3D exhibit. Analyze NASA Evidence retrieves related studies and identifies gaps between selected conditions and available evidence. The visual responses illustrate concepts in a fun appealing way; they are not calibrated predictions or a numerical combustion simulation.

Evidence lets users discover investigations, compare indexed coverage and inspect original records with their units, conditions and source locations. English and Arabic navigation help make the experience accessible.

NASA DATA AT THE CORE

We use selected material from 19 verified NASA Combustion Science Microgravity Investigations. Our indexed collection includes 41 source files, 21 CSV tables, 2,001 source rows and 12,160 scalar records, alongside 62 reviewed report passages and 61 official metadata passages. Metadata retains its discovery role rather than becoming measurement evidence. Ten supporting NASA resources remain separate from experimental evidence. These counts describe selective coverage, not complete ingestion of NASA PSI.

Our team’s pipeline preserves raw sources and manifests through format-specific extraction, conservative normalization, structured measurements, text chunking, quality checks and versioned outputs. Values, units, experimental conditions and source locations remain traceable. Unknown units stay unknown.

CREATIVITY AND IMPACT

FLARE UP connects an immersive visual exhibit to inspectable NASA research. Users move from curiosity to a question, then follow the answer back to its source. We considered scientific validity, accessibility, clear uncertainty, multilingual use, visual simplicity and practical demo reliability. Our goal is to make spacecraft combustion research easier to understand and explore, not to provide operational fire-safety recommendations.

TOOLS AND DEVELOPMENT

We built the interface with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS and Three.js. Python and FastAPI power local lexical and latent-semantic retrieval and separate structured searches. Groq-hosted openai/gpt-oss-20b provides optional grounded synthesis. Netlify and Render host the application. We validated text, structured and hybrid routes, multilingual retrieval, corpus safeguards and the Lab’s sample categories, including 41 offline tests. Free hosting may require a wake-up period, and automated checks do not replace expert scientific review.

Explore the project: https://flare-up-ranad0.netlify.app/

Source code and acknowledgements: https://github.com/ranad0/FLARE-UP
